---
title: "🌊 Fishing area analysis"
description: >
  fao_areas() and fishing_area_map(): the FAO major fishing areas and their subareas;
  fishing_area_data(), fishing_area_species() and fishing_area_country(): total catch,
  main species and main countries of an FAO fishing area, with all options.
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
source("_setup.R")
```

```{r data-source, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
data_source()
```

`fao_areas()` and `fishing_area_map()` show the FAO major fishing areas and their subareas; the
three other fishing area functions describe one area. The examples use the **Northeast Atlantic
(area 27)**; the last section shows the same analysis for the **Northwest Atlantic (area 21)**.

## 🗺️ The FAO major fishing areas

The FAO major fishing areas for statistical purposes are defined by the Coordinating Working
Party on Fishery Statistics (CWP): 19 marine areas, and the inland waters of each continent.
`fao_areas()` lists them with their catch in the last year of the data and the link to the
official FAO map of each area, and saves a world map of the marine areas labelled with their
codes:

```{r, figures = TRUE}
areas <- fao_areas()
```

```{r}
show_table(areas[order(-areas$catch_last_year), c("area_code", "name_en", "type", "ocean", "catch_last_year", "share_pct")],
           n = 30, digits = 1)
```

Use these names (e.g. `"Atlantic, Northwest"`) or codes in the other functions. The official FAO
maps (column `fao_map`) are the maps of the
[FAO fishing area maps](https://www.fao.org/fishery/docs/maps/Default.htm) page; the package
links to them.

## 🧭 `fishing_area_map()`: an area and its subareas

Large areas are divided into subareas, divisions and subdivisions; in the Northeast Atlantic
they are the ICES areas, from 27.1 (Barents Sea) to 27.14 (East Greenland). `fishing_area_map()`
maps one marine area with these units, labelled with their codes, from the boundaries bundled
with the package (FAO 2024). When the
[ggOceanMaps](https://github.com/MikkoVihtakari/ggOceanMaps) package (Vihtakari 2026) is
installed, the map is drawn on its bathymetric base map, with the depth of the ETOPO 2022
relief model (NOAA NCEI 2022) bundled with ggOceanMaps; areas reaching beyond 60° of latitude,
such as area 27, are drawn in a polar stereographic projection. Without ggOceanMaps, the land
of Natural Earth is drawn in a Lambert azimuthal equal-area projection centred on the area.

```{r, figures = "subarea_map"}
ne_atlantic <- fishing_area_map(27)
```

```{r}
show_table(ne_atlantic$units, n = 20)
ne_atlantic$fao_map      # the official FAO map of the area
```

The sources of the map are in `ne_atlantic$sources`, to cite with it:

```{r}
show_table(ne_atlantic$sources)
```

The divisions, here without depth:

```{r, figures = "division_map"}
fishing_area_map(27, level = "division", bathymetry = FALSE)
```

All arguments of `fishing_area_map()`:

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `area` | FAO major marine fishing area: code (e.g. `27`) or English name | |
| `level` | Units drawn inside the area: `"subarea"`, `"division"`, `"subdivision"` or `"none"` (outline only) | `"subarea"` |
| `bathymetry` | Show the depth (ggOceanMaps only) | `TRUE` |
| `labels` | Label the units with their codes | `TRUE` |
| `engine` | `"auto"` (ggOceanMaps when installed, else `"sf"`), `"ggOceanMaps"` or `"sf"` | `"auto"` |
| `plot` | Save the map in `figures/png/area/` | `TRUE` |
| `table` | Save the table of units in `tables/` | `TRUE` |
| `lang` | Language of the map text: `"en"`, `"zh"` or `"both"` | `NULL`: the language of `fao_settings()` |
| `pptx` | Also save the map as an editable PowerPoint file | `FALSE`, or `pptx` of `fao_settings()` |
| `plot_show` | Also draw each chart in the plot window (e.g. the Plots pane of RStudio) as it is saved | `FALSE`, or `plot_show` of `fao_settings()` |

## 1️⃣ `fishing_area_data()`: catch of the area

```{r, figures = TRUE}
FAO27 <- fishing_area_data("Atlantic, Northeast")
```

It saves three charts in `figures/png/`:

| File | Chart |
|---|---|
| `fishing_trend.png` | Total catch of the area. With `timeseries_analysis = TRUE`, the grey horizontal lines are the mean catch of each period between **breakpoints**, and the dashed lines mark the start of each period (see [How the breakpoints are found](#breakpoints)) |
| `fishing_percentage.png` | The area's share of the world catch of all marine areas each year (for an inland area: of the world catch of all inland waters), and the average of these shares (red line) |
| `area_country_map.png` | Total catch of each country in the area over all years, on a world map |

and returns a list:

| Element | Content |
|---|---|
| `area_data` | Catch records of the area (all eight columns of the data): the input of the other functions |
| `coefs_data` | Periods between breakpoints of the total catch: `start_year`, `end_year` and `intercept` (mean catch of the period, in tonnes) |
| `act_world_map` | The map data, an sf object with the total catch of each country (`NULL` with `plot = FALSE`) |

```{r}
FAO27$coefs_data
```

### Options

```{r, figures = TRUE}
fishing_area_data(
  "Atlantic, Northeast",
  timeseries_analysis = FALSE,          # no breakpoints
  area_color1 = "#9ecae1",              # fill of the catch area
  area_color2 = "#08519c",              # its outline
  hline_color = "#e6550d",              # average line of the share chart
  fill_scale = "blue",                  # palette of the map
  lang = "zh"                           # Chinese chart text
)
```

All arguments of `fishing_area_data()`:

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `area_name` | FAO major fishing area, as named in the data (table above) | |
| `plot` | Save the three charts; `FALSE` only returns the data | `TRUE` |
| `timeseries_analysis` | Draw the breakpoints and the mean catch of each period on the total catch chart (`coefs_data` is returned either way) | `TRUE` |
| `area_color1` | Fill colour of the total catch | `"grey80"` |
| `area_alpha` | Transparency of that fill (0 transparent to 1 opaque) | `0.7` |
| `area_color2` | Outline colour of the total catch | `"black"` |
| `line_color` | Colour of the line of the share chart | `"black"` |
| `line_alpha` | Transparency of that line | `0.8` |
| `line_linewidth` | Width of that line | `1.5` |
| `point_size` | Size of the points of the share chart | `2` |
| `hline_color` | Colour of the average line of the share chart | `"red"` |
| `hline_alpha` | Transparency of the average line | `0.7` |
| `hline_linewidth` | Width of the average line | `1.5` |
| `axis_text_size` | Size of the axis labels of the share chart, and of the axis titles of the total catch chart | `10` |
| `axis_text_face` | Font face of the axis titles of the total catch chart: `"plain"`, `"bold"`, `"italic"` or `"bold.italic"` | `"plain"` |
| `axis_title_size` | Size of the axis titles of the share chart | `12` |
| `axis_title_face` | Font face of the axis titles of the share chart and the map | `"bold"` |
| `strip_text_size`, `strip_text_face` | Size and font face of panel titles; the charts of this function have no panels, so they have no visible effect | `12`, `"bold"` |
| `polygon_color` | Colour of the country borders on the map | `"grey90"` |
| `fill_scale` | Palette of the map, any choice of `map_palette` in `fao_settings()` (e.g. `"blue"`, `"YlOrRd"`, `"viridis"` or a vector of colours) | `NULL`: `map_palette` of `fao_settings()` (`"deep-orange"`) |
| `axis_title_size_map` | Size of the axis titles of the map | `14` |
| `axis_text_size_map` | Size of the axis labels (longitudes and latitudes) of the map | `12` |
| `legend_text_size_map` | Size of the legend text of the map | `12` |
| `ZH` | Older way of asking for Chinese: `TRUE` is `lang = "zh"` | `FALSE` |
| `lang` | Language of the chart text: `"en"`, `"zh"` or `"both"` | `NULL`: `"zh"` if `ZH = TRUE`, else the language of `fao_settings()` |
| `data_version` | FAO release: `"latest"` (newest available), `"bundled"` or a release such as `"2026.1.0"` (see [💾 FAO data](data.html)) | `"latest"` |
| `pptx` | Also save the charts as editable PowerPoint files in `figures/pptx/` | `FALSE`, or `pptx` of `fao_settings()` |
| `plot_show` | Also draw each chart in the plot window (e.g. the Plots pane of RStudio) as it is saved | `FALSE`, or `plot_show` of `fao_settings()` |

## 2️⃣ `fishing_area_species()`: main species

```{r, figures = TRUE}
species <- fishing_area_species(FAO27$area_data, rank_range = 1:10)
```

| File | Chart |
|---|---|
| `area/area_species.png` | Catch of the selected species over time |
| `area/area_species_wrap.png` | One panel per species with its share of the area's catch over all years, a linear trend (dashed) and the breakpoints of its mean catch; with `timeseries_analysis = FALSE`, a smooth curve instead of the trend and breakpoints |

The function returns a list:

| Element | Content |
|---|---|
| `area_species` | Catch of every species item by year |
| `area_species_ranked` | Catch by year of the selected species, with their total catch and share |
| `area_species_ranked_total` | The selected species: total catch over all years (`Total_Tonnes`) and share of the area's catch (`Percentage`) |
| `coefs_data` | Breakpoints of each species: `start_year`, `end_year` and `intercept` (mean catch of the period, in tonnes) |

```{r}
show_table(species$area_species_ranked_total)
```

It also saves two tables in `tables/`: `species_ranked_table.csv` (average catch per decade, catch
in each of the last five years, catch and share in the last year) and `species_coefs_data.csv`
(the breakpoints).

```{r}
show_table(read.csv("tables/species_ranked_table.csv", fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM", check.names = FALSE), n = 5, digits = 0)
```

### Options

- **`rank_range`** lists the ranks shown: `11:20` shows the next ten species, `c(5, 6)` the fifth and the sixth.
- **`timeseries_analysis = FALSE`** replaces the breakpoints by a smooth curve
  (`smooth_method`, default `"loess"`).
- **`h_value`** is the minimum length of a period between breakpoints: a fraction of the series
  (default `0.15`) or a number of years (e.g. `5`). Larger values give fewer breakpoints;
  species with too short a series are skipped with a message.

```{r, figures = TRUE}
fishing_area_species(FAO27$area_data, rank_range = 11:20, h_value = 5, lang = "both")
```

All arguments of `fishing_area_species()`. "Time series chart" is `area_species.png`, "panel
chart" is `area_species_wrap.png`; the panel chart with breakpoints has fixed line widths, text
sizes and two columns, and only the `text_*` arguments change it.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `area_data` | Catch data of an area: `fishing_area_data()$area_data` or any subset of `load_fao_data()` | |
| `rank_range` | Ranks of the species shown, by total catch over all years: `1:10` the ten largest, `11:20` the next ten, `c(5, 6)` the fifth and the sixth | `1:10` |
| `plot` | Save the charts | `TRUE` |
| `table` | Save the two tables in `tables/` | `TRUE` |
| `timeseries_analysis` | `TRUE`: panel chart with linear trend and breakpoints; `FALSE`: panel chart with a smooth curve | `TRUE` |
| `h_value` | Minimum length of a period between breakpoints: a fraction of the series or a number of years (the `h` of `strucchange::breakpoints()`) | `0.15` |
| `line_width` | Width of the lines of the time series chart | `1.5` |
| `line_alpha` | Transparency of the lines of the time series chart and of the panel chart without breakpoints | `0.7` |
| `line_linewidth` | Width of the lines of the panel chart without breakpoints | `1.5` |
| `point_size` | Size of the points of the time series chart and of the panel chart without breakpoints | `1.8` |
| `point_alpha` | Transparency of these points | `0.7` |
| `point_shape` | Shape of these points (R point symbol, e.g. `1` open circle, `16` filled circle) | `1` |
| `axis_text_size`, `axis_text_face` | Size and font face of the axis labels (time series chart; y axis of the panel chart without breakpoints) | `10`, `"plain"` |
| `axis_title_size`, `axis_title_face` | Size and font face of the axis titles (time series chart; panel chart without breakpoints) | `10`, `"bold"` |
| `strip_text_size`, `strip_text_face` | Size and font face of the panel titles of the panel chart without breakpoints | `10`, `"bold"` |
| `smooth_method` | Smoothing method of the curve in the panel chart without breakpoints, as in `ggplot2::geom_smooth()`: `"loess"`, `"lm"`, `"gam"`, ... | `"loess"` |
| `smooth_linetype` | Line type of that curve: `"dashed"`, `"solid"`, `"dotted"`, ... | `"dashed"` |
| `text_hjust`, `text_vjust` | Horizontal and vertical justification of the share label in each panel (it is anchored at 1957 and zero catch) | `0.9`, `-4` |
| `text_size`, `text_color` | Size and colour of the share label | `4.5`, `"black"` |
| `facet_ncol` | Number of columns of the panel chart without breakpoints | `2` |
| `ZH` | Older way of asking for Chinese: `TRUE` is `lang = "zh"` | `FALSE` |
| `lang` | Language of the chart text and names: `"en"`, `"zh"` or `"both"` | `NULL`: `"zh"` if `ZH = TRUE`, else the language of `fao_settings()` |
| `pptx` | Also save the charts as editable PowerPoint files in `figures/pptx/` | `FALSE`, or `pptx` of `fao_settings()` |
| `plot_show` | Also draw each chart in the plot window (e.g. the Plots pane of RStudio) as it is saved | `FALSE`, or `plot_show` of `fao_settings()` |

## 3️⃣ `fishing_area_country()`: main countries

```{r, figures = TRUE}
countries <- fishing_area_country(FAO27$area_data, rank_range = 1:10)
```

It works like `fishing_area_species()`, by country:

| Output | Content |
|---|---|
| `area/area_country.png` | Catch of the selected countries over time |
| `area/area_country_wrap.png` | One panel per country with its share of the area's catch, a linear trend and the breakpoints (or a smooth curve) |
| `tables/country_ranked_table.csv` | Average catch per decade, catch in each of the last five years, catch and share in the last year |
| `tables/country_coefs_data.csv` | The breakpoints |
| Returned list | `area_country` (catch of every country by year), `area_country_ranked`, `area_country_ranked_total` and `coefs_data` |

```{r}
show_table(countries$area_country_ranked_total)
```

All arguments of `fishing_area_country()`. As for the species, the panel chart with breakpoints
has fixed line widths, text sizes and two columns.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `area_data` | Catch data of an area: `fishing_area_data()$area_data` or any subset of `load_fao_data()` | |
| `rank_range` | Ranks of the countries shown, by total catch over all years: `1:10` the ten largest, `c(5, 6)` the fifth and the sixth | `1:10` |
| `plot` | Save the charts | `TRUE` |
| `table` | Save the two tables in `tables/` | `TRUE` |
| `timeseries_analysis` | `TRUE`: panel chart with linear trend and breakpoints; `FALSE`: panel chart with a smooth curve | `TRUE` |
| `h_value` | Minimum length of a period between breakpoints: a fraction of the series or a number of years | `0.15` |
| `line_width` | Width of the lines of the time series chart (`area_country.png`) | `1.5` |
| `line_alpha` | Transparency of the lines of the time series chart and of the panel chart without breakpoints | `0.7` |
| `line_linewidth` | Width of the lines of the panel chart without breakpoints | `1.5` |
| `point_size` | Size of the points of the time series chart and of the panel chart without breakpoints | `1.8` |
| `point_alpha` | Transparency of these points | `0.7` |
| `point_shape` | Shape of these points (R point symbol) | `1` |
| `axis_text_size`, `axis_text_face` | Size and font face of the axis labels (time series chart; y axis of the panel chart without breakpoints) | `10`, `"plain"` |
| `axis_title_size`, `axis_title_face` | Size and font face of the axis titles (time series chart; panel chart without breakpoints) | `10`, `"bold"` |
| `strip_text_size`, `strip_text_face` | Size and font face of the panel titles of the panel chart without breakpoints | `10`, `"bold"` |
| `smooth_method` | Smoothing method of the curve in the panel chart without breakpoints, as in `ggplot2::geom_smooth()` | `"loess"` |
| `smooth_linetype` | Line type of that curve | `"dashed"` |
| `text_hjust`, `text_vjust` | Justification of the share label in each panel | `0.9`, `-4` |
| `text_size`, `text_color` | Size and colour of the share label | `4.5`, `"black"` |
| `facet_ncol` | Number of columns of the panel chart without breakpoints | `2` |
| `ZH` | Older way of asking for Chinese: `TRUE` is `lang = "zh"` | `FALSE` |
| `lang` | Language of the chart text and names: `"en"`, `"zh"` or `"both"` | `NULL`: `"zh"` if `ZH = TRUE`, else the language of `fao_settings()` |
| `pptx` | Also save the charts as editable PowerPoint files | `FALSE`, or `pptx` of `fao_settings()` |
| `plot_show` | Also draw each chart in the plot window (e.g. the Plots pane of RStudio) as it is saved | `FALSE`, or `plot_show` of `fao_settings()` |

## 📐 How the breakpoints are found {#breakpoints}

The breakpoints divide a catch series into periods with different mean catch. Each series is
fitted with a model of constant mean (`catch ~ 1`) in each period; the breakpoints that minimise
the residual sum of squares are found by dynamic programming (Bai and Perron 2003), and the
number of breakpoints is chosen by the Bayesian information criterion (BIC), as done by
`strucchange::breakpoints()` (Zeileis et al. 2002, 2003). Every period has at least `h` years:
15% of the series in `fishing_area_data()`, and `h_value` in the other functions.

| Function | Series analysed |
|---|---|
| `fishing_area_data()` | Total catch of the area in each year |
| `fishing_area_species()` | Catch of each species, over its longest run of consecutive years |
| `fishing_area_country()` | Catch of each country, over all years with records (a warning is given when years are missing) |

The breakpoints show when the level of the catch changed, not why: changes in fishing, in the
stocks, in markets or in reporting can all move the catch.

## 🌏 Another area: the Northwest Atlantic

Any FAO area works the same way. The Northwest Atlantic (area 21) lies off Canada, the United
States and Greenland:

```{r, figures = TRUE}
FAO21 <- fishing_area_data("Atlantic, Northwest")
fishing_area_country(FAO21$area_data, rank_range = 1:8)
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
area21 <- FAO21$area_data
total21 <- tapply(area21$Production, area21$Year, sum, na.rm = TRUE)
is_cod <- area21$ASFIS.species..Name. == "Atlantic cod"
cod21 <- tapply(area21$Production[is_cod], area21$Year[is_cod], sum, na.rm = TRUE)
mt21 <- function(x) formatC(x / 1e6, format = "f", digits = 1)
kt21 <- function(x) formatC(x / 1e3, format = "f", digits = 0)
```

The catch of area 21 was largest in `r names(which.max(total21))` (`r mt21(max(total21))` million
t) and was `r mt21(total21[[length(total21)]])` million t in `r names(total21)[length(total21)]`.
Its Atlantic cod fell from `r kt21(cod21[["1990"]])` thousand t in 1990 to
`r kt21(cod21[["1995"]])` thousand t in 1995: the cod off Newfoundland and Labrador collapsed, and
Canada closed the fishery in 1992 (Hutchings and Myers 1994).

::: callout-tip
Charts of different areas are saved under the same file names (e.g. `fishing_trend.png`), so
use one working folder per area, e.g. `setwd("reports/FAO21")`.
:::
